messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-12 09:12 -0700
Subject: Offer level discrepancy for Sofia Ramos — need HR guidance

Hi Laura / Naomi,

Quick thread to surface a discrepancy on the Sofia Ramos offer before we send it. Interview panel recommended IC3 (Sr SW Eng) with consistent feedback on system design, ownership, and shipping quality. Compensation team (recruiting comp ops) is planning to issue an IC2 offer citing comp ranges for the role and current internal parity.

Sofia is a high-priority hire for the infra team — she has 6.5 years, led a small infra team at GreenLeaf, and her take-home test showed very strong architectural judgment. Panel notes attached (interview_panel_notes.pdf).

Can HR confirm whether we can extend IC3 for this req? If not, what documented criteria would we need to override? I want to avoid wasting candidate time with back-and-forth.

Proposed asks:
- Laura: Can you advise on approved flex for IC3 in this requisition?
- Naomi: Can you hold the candidate communication until we align?

I can provide written panel justification or pull up the calibration notes if that helps.

Thanks,
Rachel
Rachel Kim
Hiring Manager, Infrastructure
Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-12 10:03 -0700
Subject: Re: Offer level discrepancy for Sofia Ramos — need HR guidance

Thanks for the context, Rachel — I reviewed the panel notes and the current comp grid for the IC tracks. Short answer: there is limited approved flexibility for IC3 on this req because the headcount was opened as IC2 with budget tied to the hiring plan for Q3. That said, we do have a documented escalation path for exceptions if the hiring manager can provide concrete evidence of difference in scope/impact.

What we need to approve an IC3:
- A 1-paragraph summary of why the role's expected scope will exceed IC2 (customer impact, ownership, cross-team responsibilities).
- Consolidated interviewer feedback with 3–4 datapoints showing IC3-level skills (I've reviewed the attached notes — please extract the strongest quotes).
- Confirmation from Eng Director (Marissa CC'd) that this headcount should be reclassified for scope/band reasons.

If approved, comp will need to come from the discretionary uplift bucket for the team and CS/finance sign-off. Please attach the short summary here and I will run it in today's exceptions slot.

I attached the comp policy excerpt for visibility (comp_range_policy.pdf).

Laura
Laura Bennett
Sr. Manager, Talent Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Offer level discrepancy for Sofia Ramos — need HR guidance

Laura — thanks. Attaching consolidated panel highlights below (also attached as PDF). Short summary (one paragraph) follows and I’ll add a couple interviewer quotes.

Role scope rationale:
Sofia was hired by GreenLeaf to lead reliability improvements across multiple services and was the primary owner for a migration that reduced tail latency by 30% for their API surface. At Redwood, we intend for this position to own platform reliability across the new streaming router and to lead cross-team efforts on KV cache consistency; that level of cross-team ownership and mentorship corresponds to IC3 impact.

Top interviewer datapoints:
- "Led a cross-functional migration with measurable 30% latency improvement; demonstrates end-to-end execution and stakeholder management." (Panelist A)
- "Design answers consistently showed tradeoffs between latency, cost, and operational complexity; strong product sense." (Panelist B)
- "Mentorship and hiring experience noted; ran an on-call rotation redesign at GreenLeaf." (Panelist C)

Naomi — please hold candidate comms. Sofia is available for an offer discussion tomorrow afternoon; we should be ready to present the correct level and comp.

Rachel

Thanks for pulling this together, Rachel — good write-up and useful datapoints. I reviewed the panel highlights and the proposed scope. I agree Sofia's expected role at Redwood is IC3 given the cross-team ownership and the migration leadership examples.

Decision and next steps:
- Approved: escalate this req to IC3. Laura: please mark the headcount reclassification and flag comp for discretionary uplift. Naomi: please prepare an IC3 offer package (base + sign-on) within the IC3 midpoint and aim to keep within the discretionary uplift cap; loop Finance if the request exceeds the cap.
- Rachel: please confirm the final target base and sign-on expectations for Sofia so Naomi can finalize. If we need to move beyond the discretionary bucket, Finance escalation will be required and could add 24–48 hours.
- Candidate communication: Naomi, you have permission to schedule the offer call for tomorrow 2pm PT. Please keep the wording neutral on banding and present the role and comp.

Laura — I will sign off on the exception request once you route it; if comp looks within the uplift band no additional approvals needed.

Marissa
VP, Engineering
Redwood Inference
